newsitem.title: CHINA: Nearly one-third of Chinese unhappy with prices.
newsitem.headline: Nearly one-third of Chinese unhappy with prices.

text.p: Nearly one-third of China's people think current prices are too high to bear, according to a survey published in the Financial News on Friday.

The survey by the People's Bank of China, the central bank, questioned 20,727 people in China's major 34 cities, the newspaper said. About 30.6 percent said prices were unbearably high, a drop of 1.8 percentage points compared with the previous survey, the survey showed.
It revealed that people's incomes were a major factor in whether they said prices were unbearably high, or just stable, it said.
About 41.5 percent of retired people and 37.1 percent of farmers said prices were too high, or 11 percentage points and seven percentage points higher respectively than the average, it said.
China's benchmark retail price inflation was 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent in 1995 and from a communist-era high of 21.7 percent in 1994.
Retail price inflation in February was a year-on-year 2.9 percent.
